name: Eastern Plains - Inland and North of Western Australia

climate: Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.

land: The high ground runs about 5°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
